title: An Option That Can Help Cut Housing Prices Catches On
partialText: Preapproved plans trim weeks or months off the process of getting a building permit. “Every month of delay adds costs that ultimately land on the buyer,” one housing expert said.

title: Giving Workers a Stake in A.I. Gains Traction
partialText: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California has floated a policy idea that’s getting attention in Silicon Valley: let workers own a piece of technology disruption.

title: Stocks and Oil Prices Tick Up Amid Impasse Over Reopening Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Nearly three months since the fighting began, disagreements remain over the fate of Iran’s uranium stockpile and transit fees for the Strait of Hormuz.

title: StreetEasy’s ‘Reserve Your Future’ Is Taking Reservations for 2046
partialText: To celebrate 20 years in business, a New York real-estate site is offering restaurant reservations two decades in the future, an unusual offer in a city of short shelf lives.

title: With Gas Prices Through the Roof, Will Renting an EV or Hybrid Car Save You Money?
partialText: With gas prices through the roof, more travelers are considering alternative vehicles to control costs. But how much will you really save?

title: Guy Savoy Awarded Légion d’Honneur
partialText: Guy Savoy, who worked his way up from modest beginnings (and a recent setback), this week became the first chef inducted into the prestigious Académie des Beaux-Arts.

title: Move Over, Private Equity. It’s Great to Be a Banker Again.
partialText: They played second fiddle to private equity and hedge funds for years, but 2026 is shaping up to be “the year of the bank,” one consultant said.

title: Superman Experience at Warner Bros. Mirrors Hollywood’s Change
partialText: Inside the reworked Stage 5, a hallowed soundstage where John Wayne once roamed and the cast of “Friends” sipped coffee on couches.

title: Asian Currencies Hit by Iran War, Adding to Economic Strain
partialText: Soaring oil prices and a surging dollar are testing Asia’s foreign-exchange reserves, which were built up after the 1997 crisis.

title: U.S. Invests $2 Billion and Takes Stake in Quantum Firms
partialText: The Trump administration said it had signed preliminary deals for equity stakes in nine quantum computing companies.

title: Audit Immunity for Trump Family Puts I.R.S. in a Bind
partialText: Federal law prohibits the Internal Revenue Service from halting an audit at the direction of the president or his aides.

title: ‘Peanuts’ Music Owner Sues Interior Department and 3 Companies for Copyright Infringement
partialText: The owner of the “Peanuts” catalog would really like it if companies and the U.S. government stopped using its music without permission.

title: Mortgage Rates, Now 6.5%, Hit Highest Level Since War Began
partialText: The average rate on a 30-year mortgage rose amid growing concerns over inflation and as the war with Iran showed no sign of ending.

title: Elon Musk and Other CEOs on Trump’s Trip to China Sought Relief
partialText: Elon Musk and other powerful executives who accompanied President Trump to China are hoping to clear roadblocks put up by Beijing.

title: French Court Says Air France and Airbus Are Guilty in 2009 Crash Case
partialText: An appeals court in Paris said the airline and airplane manufacturer were guilty of involuntary manslaughter for their role in a plane crash over the Atlantic Ocean.

title: 2 Minnesota Autism Therapy Providers Charged in $46 Million Medicaid Fraud Case
partialText: The Justice Department claims that clinics used fake diagnoses and kickbacks to parents to bring children into treatment.

title: Trump Cancels Signing of Executive Order Granting Oversight of A.I. Models
partialText: The president said he postponed the executive order, which would give the government power to evaluate A.I. models before their release, over concerns about “aspects of it.”

title: SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic Race to Go Public
partialText: SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic, giants of the artificial intelligence sector, are rushing to test investor appetite in the stock markets.

title: Goldman Hits the Jackpot After Banks’ ‘Dogfight’ to Lead SpaceX’s I.P.O.
partialText: Across Wall Street, bankers have been clamoring to lead what is expected to be the biggest-ever initial public offering.

title: Walmart Shares Sink as Investors Fret About Price-Conscious Shoppers
partialText: The nation’s largest retailer reported a rise in sales, but consumers are seeking out low-price items and cutting back in some categories, a potentially worrying sign for the U.S. economy.

title: Experimental Drug Yields Dramatic Weight Loss
partialText: People who got the injection, retatrutide, lost 28 percent of their body weight on average after 80 weeks, Eli Lilly said.

title: Samsung Averts a Walkout With Big Bonuses, but Discord Over A.I. Profits Brews
partialText: Samsung Electronics, a global memory chip supplier, has been a major beneficiary of the A.I boom. It has also become the center of a debate over how to divide its spoils.

title: British Politics Is Obsessing Over the Bond Market. Here’s Why.
partialText: Britain is facing another round of turmoil in government leadership, jolting debt investors who were already on high alert over inflation.

title: Bluesky Says Kremlin Is Hacking Its Platform to Spread Propaganda
partialText: The company said it was fighting Russian efforts to hijack real users’ accounts to post fake content, an apparently novel tactic.

title: Trump Approved a Nvidia Chip for Sale in China. Beijing Doesn’t Want It.
partialText: The U.S. tech giant’s powerful H200 chip seemed poised to boost Beijing’s A.I. ambitions, but not a single one has been purchased in China.

title: China’s Endless Housing Crisis Shows Faint Signs of Hope
partialText: Property prices in Shanghai, in particular, are rebounding, but the national market still faces an enormous overhang — 90 million empty or unfinished apartments.

title: Musk’s SpaceX Reveals Its Finances for the First Time as It Readies for IPO
partialText: Mr. Musk’s rocket and satellite maker disclosed its financial performance as it prepares to go public in what is set to be one of the largest offerings to date.

title: T.S.A. Pushes to Expand Private Security at Airports with ‘Gold+’ Program
partialText: Driven in part by the chaos of the last shutdown, the government is expanding efforts to use private security staff instead of federal employees at more airports.

title: Nvidia’s Profit Hits $58.3 Billion as A.I. Boom Gathers More Steam
partialText: The chip maker said its profit in its most recent quarter jumped 211 percent from a year earlier thanks to extreme demand from other big technology companies.

title: Majority of Fed Officials Embraced Possibility of Higher Rates at Latest Meeting
partialText: A record of the April meeting, Jerome H. Powell’s last as chair, underscored the extent to which the war with Iran has upended the economic outlook.

title: Jeff Bezos Praises Trump’s Second Term as ‘More Mature’
partialText: The Amazon founder and owner of The Washington Post also rejected the idea that he has made changes at his companies to gain favor with the president.

title: Barney Frank, Gay Pioneer and Liberal Stalwart in Congress, Dies at 86
partialText: Often voted the “brainiest,” “funniest” and “most eloquent” member of the House, he was also the first to come out voluntarily and helped normalize being openly gay in public office.

title: To 2026 Graduates Facing a Bleak Job Market, 1991 Grads Have Some Advice
partialText: The New York Times profiled young job seekers in 1991. Today, their own children are entering a work force in flux.

partialText: The media scion is buying Vox Media’s podcast network, New York magazine and Vox.com for more than $300 million.

title: The Growing Anxiety Over AI, Jobs and the Future
partialText: Layoffs linked to artificial intelligence are rattling workers and college graduates, stoking concerns worldwide that are showing up in polls.

title: Is the Bond Market Signaling Danger? Or Opportunity?
partialText: Interest rates for long-term Treasury bonds have surged to levels last seen in 2007, before the great financial crisis.

title: A Founder of e.l.f. Cosmetics Gave Up the High Life to Be a Catholic Priest
partialText: A mystical encounter 12 years ago led Scott Vincent Borba, a founder of E.L.F. Beauty, on a journey that will culminate this week, when he is ordained as a Roman Catholic priest.

title: China Confirms It Will Buy 200 Boeing Planes
partialText: Beijing’s acknowledgment on Wednesday that tariffs were discussed in talks with President Trump signals it was prepared to push back if the U.S. revives duties.

title: Trump’s Stock Trades Raise Eyebrows. The Family Says He Keeps His Hands Off.
partialText: The Trump Organization says the president’s financial investments are handled by outside firms and that it has no control over the timing or selection of transactions.

title: Tickle Me Elmo and the ‘Elmo-Mania’ That Consumed America

title: Greg Hyman, Co-Creator of Tickle Me Elmo, Dies at 78
partialText: An electronics wizard, he was already a veteran inventor when he collaborated with Ron Dubren on an idea for a toy that giggled. The rest is retail history.

title: Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2007 as Inflation Fears Set In
partialText: The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield hasn’t been this high since the lead-up to the global financial crisis. Across Europe and Asia, yields are also elevated.

title: Powered by A.I., Google Changes Its Search Box for the First Time in 25 Years
partialText: Using a new Gemini A.I. model, the tech giant is overhauling its search box dimensions to answer longer queries, adding a video-generation tool and simplifying online shopping.

title: Son of Mango Fashion Chain’s Founder Is Arrested as Suspect in His Death
partialText: Isak Andic, the billionaire who built the Spanish brand, died while hiking with his son in 2024. News outlets had reported that the son was under investigation.

title: Inflation Fears Cloud G7 Economic Agenda as Iran War Persists

title: Rising Energy Costs and Data Centers at Heart of NextEra’s Dominion Bid

title: Amazon E-Bikes Take Root in Manhattan and Brooklyn
partialText: Small companies that handle the final delivery are relying on them to skirt New York City traffic. Amazon plans to try the bikes elsewhere, too.

title: China Wants A.I. to Flourish, but Not at the Expense of Jobs
partialText: A series of precedent-setting rulings signals that Chinese courts are being enlisted to shield workers from displacement by artificial intelligence.

title: Tesla’s Semi Truck could Jolt the Trucking Industry
partialText: California truckers have expressed strong interest in the Tesla Semi because it costs much less and can travel further on a charge than electric trucks sold by established manufacturers.
